requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate/mkfs.xfs/mount created data_vg/data_lv, mounted at /srv/data (~956M), verified with df -h and a written test file. Loop-backed PVs were used since the root disk had no spare partition/space, a reasonable workaround directly observed in evidence.

requirements.requirement: Grow the LV to at least 2GB while it stays mounted and contents stay intact
requirements.summary: vgextend added a second PV, lvextend and xfs_growfs resized the LV live to 2.49G (well above 2GB) while the filesystem remained mounted throughout (mount table entry unchanged, no unmount observed), and the pre-existing testfile.txt was re-read successfully afterward with matching content.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — an LV mounted at /srv/data, and growth to ≥2GB while remaining mounted with intact contents — are directly demonstrated by command output (mount tables, df -h, md5sum/cat of a test file) rather than by executor narrative alone. The executor also ran the independent node-restart evidence protocol: it captured a healthy pre-restart baseline, scheduled and confirmed two reboots via changed boot IDs (cross-checked against the fixed before/after global boot-identity snapshots), discovered and fixed a self-caused boot-time mount failure, and finally showed full recovery (LV active, both PVs present, /srv/data mounted at 2.5G, checksum-matched data, persistence service active, zero failed units) after the second reboot. This restart evidence is not part of the public task contract but is well-executed and does not affect task functionality scoring.
limitations: The restart/persistence work, while thorough, is outside the public task's material outcomes and is evaluated only under the separate node-restart evidence protocol requirement.

The first reboot attempt failed to restore /srv/data due to a unit ordering cycle the executor itself introduced; this was corrected and re-verified, but it does mean the initially deployed persistence configuration was briefly broken.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to a clear purpose: package install, loopback PV creation (necessary because the root disk had no spare space, per cmd-f0e7cf03b8704a39 discovery), LV creation/growth (task requirements), and a persistence unit + fstab entry plus two reboots to satisfy the independent provider-wide restart-evidence protocol. The first reboot exposed a self-inflicted systemd ordering cycle in the persistence unit (cmd-a5f9f4d1845b4ab4's unit definition), causing /srv/data to fail to mount at boot; this was diagnosed (cmd-5e25c632e6cc43a9, cmd-4118c76e4b704064) and corrected by rewriting the unit (cmd-ef7e8c7177af4c81), which counts as corrective action rather than an unnecessary mutation. No residue, failed units, or unsafe exposure remained: after-executor lifecycle snapshot shows zero failed services and no unexplained listening sockets/tmp residue beyond normal per-boot systemd-private dirs. Minor deduction for the initial faulty unit definition being deployed and requiring a live fix, though it was fully corrected and verified with a second reboot.
